author: HSinghHira
tagline: Your ultimate IPTV & stream management companion
description:
Dispatcharr is an open-source powerhouse for managing IPTV streams, EPG data, and VOD content — think of it as the *arr family's IPTV cousin, built for streamers who want reliability and flexibility.
**Features**
- Consolidate multiple IPTV/M3U and Xtream Codes sources into a
  single, organized interface

- Stream proxy with real-time client management and automatic
  failover between backup sources

- HDHomeRun tuner emulation so Plex, Emby, and Jellyfin discover
  Dispatcharr as a live TV source

- EPG matching and generation, with XMLTV, M3U, Xtream Codes,
  and HDHomeRun output formats

- FFmpeg-based output profiles to transcode and standardize
  streams per client (e.g. AC3 for media servers, AAC for
  browsers)

- Video on Demand support with IMDB/TMDB metadata
- Multi-user accounts with granular permissions and
  network-based access restrictions

- Plugin system for custom automations and integrations
- Runs in All-in-One (AIO) mode: PostgreSQL and Redis are
  bundled inside the container, with persistent storage under
  /DATA/AppData/$AppID

**How to use?**
1. Open Dispatcharr from the ZimaAppStore dashboard.
2. Complete the initial setup and create your administrator
   account. If you're accessing the setup page from your local
   network this works out of the box.

3. Add your IPTV sources under Settings → M3U & EPG Manager
   (M3U playlist and/or Xtream Codes accounts, plus EPG
   sources).

4. Create channels from your imported streams and match them to
   EPG data, either automatically or manually.

5. Grab the generated M3U and XMLTV EPG URLs (or add Dispatcharr
   as an HDHomeRun tuner) in Plex, Emby, Jellyfin, or any other
   compatible client.

6. Further configuration — stream profiles, output profiles,
   users/permissions, DVR, and plugins — is all done afterward
   from the in-app Settings pages, without needing to rebuild
   the container.

tips.before_install:
1. This app runs in All-in-One (AIO) mode: PostgreSQL and
   Redis run inside the same container, so there's nothing
   external to provision first.

2. There are no required CHANGEME_* placeholders for a normal
   install — the default environment variables work
   out-of-the-box on a local network.

3. Optional: if you'll only ever reach Dispatcharr from your
   home network, leave DISPATCHARR_SETUP_ALLOWED_IP and
   DISPATCHARR_TRUSTED_PROXIES commented out in the compose
   file. Only fill in DISPATCHARR_SETUP_ALLOWED_IP if you need
   to finish first-run setup from a public IP.

4. Start the Dispatcharr installation.
5. Open Dispatcharr from the ZimaAppStore dashboard once the
   container is running — first boot needs a few extra
   seconds to initialize the bundled database.

6. Complete the on-screen setup to create your administrator
   account.

7. Add your M3U/Xtream Codes and EPG sources, then build out
   channels — see the in-app Settings pages and the official
   docs (https://dispatcharr.github.io/Dispatcharr-Docs/) for
   everything else.

8. Important: DISPATCHARR_SETUP_ALLOWED_IP only governs the
   one-time first-run admin setup. If you miss the window,
   create an admin manually instead of editing this variable
   after the fact — the container's built-in note points to
   `python manage.py createsuperuser` inside the running
   container.
